one_sentence_story: A Berlin waiter forgot paid bills in seconds. His brain held open tasks tight and dropped finished ones fast.
so_what_for_you: Before dinner, write down when and where you will do each open task tomorrow. Once your brain sees a real plan on paper, it closes the tab so you can sleep.

jargon_map.plain: Unfinished tasks stay nearly twice as active in your mind as finished tasks.
jargon_map.analogy: Like an unsaved tab that keeps blinking until you click save.

jargon_map.plain: The mental tug that starts the moment you commit to a job.
jargon_map.analogy: Like a stretched rubber band waiting to snap shut.

jargon_map.plain: The front brain space that holds your open tasks right now.
jargon_map.analogy: Like a small chalk slate wiped clean once you pay.

jargon_map.plain: Writing the exact time and spot you will finish a task tomorrow.
jargon_map.analogy: Like handing your brain a claim ticket so it lets go tonight.
